lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Insurance lead-gen peers that report after TREE beat Q3 guides set the same week as TREE's own (late July). EverQuote's Q3 revenue was $218.1m (+25% YoY) against a $198-208m guide (+7% vs the midpoint), with auto +21% and home/renters +70%. MediaAlpha's revenue was $375.9m (+23%) against a $330-355m guide (+10% vs the midpoint). Insurance was 67% of TREE's Q2 revenue ($209.3m, +42%). If TREE's insurance grew sequentially like EverQuote's auto line (+10.6% Q/Q), insurance would be about $231m, and total revenue would land above the top of TREE's $325-335m guide, against a $330.3m consensus sitting at the midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insurance strength has not saved this stock. In Q2 2026 insurance revenue grew 42% and MediaAlpha beat consensus the same evening, yet TREE fell 19.6% on SMB weakness, a big adj EPS miss ($0.68 vs $1.41) and a lowered FY outlook. TREE's Q2 revenue of $313.4m missed the $315.6m consensus even though peers beat. The last 8 prints moved a median 20.9% in absolute terms.

findings.finding: The same peers' forward statements show carrier budgets still expanding into Q4. EverQuote guided Q4 revenue to $213-223m (midpoint about $218m) against a pre-report consensus of $211.9m, saying carriers 'continue to maintain strong underwriting profitability and an appetite for growth'. MediaAlpha guided Q4 revenue to $355-375m (+25% YoY at the midpoint) and said carriers are 'committing meaningful budgets in both home and auto insurance'. TREE's implied Q4 guide comes from FY2026 revenue of $1.30-1.32bn and VMM of $364-374m, which the street read as a cut in July. The peers' Q4 lines argue the insurance part of that implied Q4 is not at risk of a further cut and has room to be firmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock traded on. In July a Q3 revenue guide 2% below consensus and a lowered FY outlook (EBITDA midpoint $148.5m vs $157.9m consensus) produced -19.6%. The April 2026 print was -21.7% and March was +23.9%. Moves of about 20% in either direction follow the guide.

findings.finding: SMB lender appetite stayed strong through Q3. Enova's small-business originations were about $1.8bn (+28% YoY, up from $1.6bn in Q2), and its SMB receivables were +34% YoY at 9/30. TREE's SMB weakness was the stated cause of the July drop. Its revised guide assumes lenders recover and merchants do not, and the CFO said lender appetite on the network 'has since stabilized'. Enova's growth supports the lender side of that assumption, not the merchant-demand side.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line drove the last print: weak SMB demand plus higher costs produced -19.6% on 2026-07-29. Consumer segment revenue was $60.3m in Q2 (-4% YoY), against $66.2m in Q3 2025.

findings.finding: Peer unit economics held or improved in Q3, which argues against TREE's insurance VMM squeeze getting worse. TREE's VMM fell to 28% of revenue in Q2 from 33%, blamed on Google traffic costs and carrier competition. EverQuote's variable marketing dollars were $62.6m on $218.1m revenue (28.7%), against a guide-implied 28.3%. MediaAlpha's contribution margin rose to 15.3% from 14.9% YoY, with contribution of $57.4m above its $51.5-54.5m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July, VMM up only 4% on revenue up 25%, together with a lower FY VMM range ($364-374m vs a prior $378-395m), was part of the -19.6% move.

findings.finding: Shorts built into the print. Short interest rose from 846k shares (08-14) to 1.05-1.11m (09-30/10-15), and days to cover rose from 1.48 to 4.25, while the stock rallied about 19% off its $23.50 low to $28.07. Shorts at 7.8% of float and 4 days of volume add squeeze fuel if the guide holds. They are not crowded enough to act as a mechanism on their own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior squeeze episode on record for TREE prints. The +22.5% to +23.9% up-moves (2025-03, 2025-07, 2026-03) show the stock can gap 20% or more on a good guide.

findings.finding: There is balance-sheet room for a capital-return announcement. Net leverage fell to 1.9x and free cash flow is about $80m a year (EW preview), against a market cap of about $394m. H1 2026 operating cash flow was $40.7m, cash was $110.8m at 6/30 (up from $81.1m), and no buybacks were made in H1 2026. An authorization at the print is possible, but nothing announces one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback announcement in the last 8 prints, so there is no history on this line.

findings.finding: Toast beat the top of its own recurring gross profit guide in each 2026 quarter: Q1 $529M against $505-515M (+2.7% above top) and Q2 $595M against $565-575M (+3.5% above top). findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat by $14M above the top of the guide and the stock fell -14.74% (the guide and hardware/tariff costs were blamed). Q2 2026 beat by $20M above the top and it rose +2.93%. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026) +4.55%, Q3 2025 +9.48%. Beats alone are not reliably paid.

findings.finding: The FY2026 recurring GP guide ($2,325-2,355M) less Q1 ($529M), Q2 ($595M) and the Q3 guide ($615-625M) implies Q4 of about $576-616M, midpoint about $596M. That is about +19% on Q4 2025's $502M, against 22-24% guided for Q3 and 27-28% delivered in H1. If Q3 beats by about $20M and Q4 run-rates normally, an FY raise of $20-40M (about 1-2%) is arithmetically likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the guide. Q1 2026: FY raised, but a weak next-quarter guide and hardware cost uncertainty took it -14.74%. Q2 2026: FY raised by less than the beat (tariff refund reinvested), +2.93%.

findings.finding: US eating-and-drinking-place sales (Census, seasonally adjusted) were $92.9B in September 2026, +7.0% y/y nominal and +3.4% real. Per the National Restaurant Association these are the strongest gains in more than three and nearly four years, with real sales up six months running. That is a same-store GPV tailwind for Toast's fintech gross profit (payments about 50 bps of GPV) in Q3, after Q2 'strong same-store sales trends'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GPV per location drove the Q3 2023 slowdown narrative. No clean recent case where same-store GPV alone moved the stock; Q2 2026's +2.93% came with 'strong same-store' commentary.

findings.finding: On the Q2 2026 call the CFO said hardware memory-cost pressure will have a larger P&L impact in 2027 than 2026 ('I would expect the P&L impact in '27 to be greater than '26'). The FY2026 guide already absorbs about 150 bps from memory, mostly in H2. DRAM contract prices rose about 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026 and were forecast +58-63% in Q2 2026 (TrendForce). Early 2027 commentary on this call could therefore weigh on the forward EBITDA view.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: hardware costs and tariff uncertainty were cited for the -14.74% reaction despite a beat. Q2 2026: CFO said the memory impact was already reduced against original expectations, stock +2.93%.

findings.finding: Third-party DAU tracking points to Q3 DAU growth at or slightly above the 63.49M (+25.7%) consensus. D.A. Davidson's panel of over 170k users implied Q3 DAU growth of 25.6-27.6% y/y (August DAUs +1.3% m/m), against 23% in Q2 and a company FY assumption of about 20%. A 2026-11-03 Investing.com preview says unnamed analysts' proprietary data show October trends pointing to further DAU acceleration, which could prompt a DAU guide raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): DAUs accelerated to +23% and beat the company's expectations; the stock fell 9.41% on a moderate revenue guide. Q3 2025 (2025-11-05): DAUs +36%; the stock fell 25.49% when management prioritised users over monetization. This name has sold DAU beats.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-05) management disclosed a bonus plan that pays about $10M in cash, more if growth is higher, if Q4 2026 DAU growth reaches 25%; it is excluded from FY guidance. With tracking at 25.6-27.6% for Q3 and October reportedly accelerating, an accrual in Q3/Q4 is likely. That would push Q3 adj. EBITDA below the $76M guide and/or trim the FY 26.5% margin guide by about 0.8 points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin guides were punished: the FY26 guide with a margin squeeze (2026-02-26) fell 14.01%, and the January 2026 preliminary print plus CFO exit fell 8.45%. The Q2 raise of the EBITDA margin outlook by nearly a point did not stop a 9.41% fall.

findings.finding: Monetization lags users, which is a risk to the Q4 bookings guide. Q3 bookings were guided to only +8.9% ($307M, consensus $309.05M) and FY bookings were not raised despite DAU acceleration. In August the CEO said Max might be sunset, and a 'Super Lite' tier at about half Super's price (ads, limited Energy; $35.99/yr seen on iPhone 2026-09-06) was in test. Both are ARPU / mix headwinds to bookings per DAU going into the Q4 and 2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every one of the last five reactions (-9.41, -5.62, -14.01, -8.45, -25.49) followed a release where bookings or revenue guidance, or a monetization trade-off, disappointed while users were fine.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03/04 Duolingo and Bharti Airtel announced 12 months of Super Duolingo free for Airtel's roughly 376M Indian subscribers, activated in the Airtel Thanks app with no card. This is likely a September-onward DAU and possibly paid-subscriber lift in India at low or unknown ARPU.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior telco bundle; India is a low-ARPU market. DAU lines have not been rewarded (see finding 1).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of FX driving a reaction on this name.

findings.finding: XPEL usually beats the top of its own guide: Q1 2026 came in at $117.4m against a $112-114m guide (+3.0% over the top) and Q2 2026 at $143.1m against $135-137m (+4.5%), Q4 2025 being the exception at $122.3m against $123-125m. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 4.5% beat over the top of the guide with gross margin up bought +9.54%. Q1 2026: a 3% beat sold -11.83% on the Q2 guide and margin caveats. Q4 2025: a miss against the guide sold -6.86%. So a revenue beat alone has not been enough.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said XPEL would implement 'relatively modest price increases in some regions during Q3'. That supports Q3 revenue and the gross margin he guided to 'continue to modestly increase' from 44.1%. Competitor Eastman said performance films improved price-cost in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin expansion (42.9% to 44.1%) accompanied the +9.54% Q2 reaction. In Q1 the margin outlook was hedged as 'not guaranteed' and the stock fell 11.83%.

findings.finding: Eastman, a direct PPF and window-film competitor (LLumar/SunTek), reported on 2026-10-29, after XPEL last spoke. Its performance-films volume fell sequentially in Q3 on 'continued weakness in the automotive market, particularly in China', and 'the aftermarket for performance films remained challenged in an already very weak domestic Chinese auto market'. CPCA's final September China retail was 1.618m, down 28% year on year, against roughly -20% in Q2 per XPEL's CEO and -24% in August. XPEL China was $15.9m (11% of revenue) in Q2, and the guide assumed 'consistent' APAC trends.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China has not been a stated driver of past reactions. In Q2 the region grew 106.7%, largely from the acquisition, alongside the +9.54% move. No prior China miss is on record.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide must lap the China distributor acquisition: Q4 2025 already carried $14.0m of China revenue (+51.9% year on year) against minimal China contribution in Q3 2025. Ex-China, Q2 2026 grew about 8.7% ($127.2m against $117.0m). On that rate with China flat to down in a -20-28% market, Q4 2026 comes to roughly $129.5-131.6m. Benzinga's Q4 consensus is $132.9m, and XPEL habitually guides below consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: the Q3 guide of $137-139m was below the $139.1-141.3m consensus and the stock still rose 9.54% on the beat. May 2026: the Q2 guide plus a margin hedge brought -11.83%. February 2026: the Q1 guide of $112-114m alongside a Q4 miss brought -6.86%.
